veranderings.voor: Sy ken elke kind se naam en ook die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
veranderings.na: Sy ken elke kind se naam, ook die name van die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
veranderings.rede: As written she knows every name 'and also the children', which joins two unlike objects; the intended point is that she also knows the names of children who never borrow books.

veranderings.voor: van die eerste klok af tot die laaste een lui
veranderings.na: van die eerste tot die laaste klok
veranderings.rede: The sentence mixes a prepositional phrase (van ... af) with a clause ending in a verb (tot ... lui); the plain phrase is cleaner and keeps the meaning.
AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader sonder om te vra
veranderings.na: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader na hom toe sonder om te vra
veranderings.rede: 'nader' does not say closer to whom; 'na hom toe' makes clear the book is moved towards Sipho, which is what the sentence means.
AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi op die mat met 'n dik boek oor slange.
veranderings.na: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi met 'n dik boek oor slange op die mat.
veranderings.rede: In Afrikaans the manner phrase normally comes before the place phrase; the current order reads as if the mat has the book.

veranderings.voor: Haar keel word warm en sy
veranderings.na: Haar keel word warm, en sy
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: op die lys en jy kan
veranderings.na: op die lys, en jy kan
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, also inside direct speech.

veranderings.voor: Ruan bly staan en sê sy kry altyd die goeie boeke eerste.
veranderings.na: Ruan bly staan en sê dat sy altyd die goeie boeke eerste kry.
veranderings.rede: Right after two speech tags 'sê sy', the words 'sê sy kry' first read as 'she says'; 'dat' makes clear that Ruan is speaking about her.

veranderings.voor: Donderdag terug en dan is jy
veranderings.na: Donderdag terug, en dan is jy
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, also inside direct speech.

veranderings.voor: Sy sit haar stempel neer en sy bly stil
veranderings.na: Sy sit haar stempel neer en bly stil
veranderings.rede: The repeated subject 'sy' is unnecessary and makes the sentence wooden; dropping it gives one sentence with two verbs and needs no comma.
AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.

vlae.teks: Juffrou Adonis kyk agter haar tafel op toe Ruan se stem harder word. Sy sit haar stempel neer en sy bly stil waar sy sit. Nou tel sy die stempel weer op en gaan aan met haar werk.
vlae.rede: This paragraph steps back in time inside a present-tense story ('kyk ... op toe ...', then 'Nou'), so the order of events is hard for a Grade 4 reader to follow; fixing it means choosing a tense or moving the paragraph, which is the writer's decision and not a language change.

'Haar keel word warm' is not a usual Afrikaans way of saying someone is getting angry (more usual: 'sy word warm', 'haar wange gloei'); it may be a deliberate bodily sign of anger for this lesson, so it is left unchanged for the writer to decide.
